items.title: In a short exact sequence of finite projective modules, stable freeness of two terms forces it for the third
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma is a 2-out-of-3 statement for stably free modules over an arbitrary ring, inside a short exact sequence of finite projective modules, and its proof has to treat the three possible selections of the two stably free terms (statement lines 71-73). The case where the middle term P and the submodule P' are the stably free ones is the non-formal one: one has to display P'' as the complement of a free direct summand by rewriting P'' + (P' + R^m) + R^n in two different groupings and using the given freeness of P + R^n, rather than by cancelling free summands (proof lines 80-88). The remaining case is then dismissed by symmetry. The proof uses only that the sequence of projectives splits and the definition of stable freeness, both of which stay outside the counted span as standard prerequisites.
